THESE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 12.01.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, UMESH M ADIGA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
These appeals are directed against judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.576 of 2016 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-13 at Banahatti dated 27.11.2018.
M.F.A.No.100570 of 2019 was filed by the Insurance Company, which was arrayed as Respondent No.2 and M.F.A.No.102453 of 2019 was filed by petitioners/claimants in M.V.C.No.576 of 2016.
2. We refer the parties herein as per their ranking before the Trial Court.

3. It was the case of the claimants/petitioners No.1 to 3 before the Trial Court that on 26.09.2015,
deceased Shivanappa alias Shivappa was going in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-23-K-9128 on Terdal-Rabkavi PWD Road.
At about, 8.30 a.m., he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Backhoe loader JCB (hereinafter will be referred as JCB for sake of brevity) by its driver.
In the said accident, Shivappa sustained grievous injuries; and while undergoing treatment, he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
It was further contention of claimants before the Trial Court that deceased was aged about 45 years; He was an agriculturist and earning Rs.4,00,000/- per annum.
Claimants being his wife and two sons were depending upon his earnings.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.25,50,000/-.
4. Respondent No.1 has contended before the Trial Court that accident was not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of JCB by its driver.
The said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2, it be directed to pay the compensation.

5. Respondent No.2 has denied all the averments in the petition and it has contended that the owner of the vehicle has violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance and therefore, it was not liable to pay the compensation.
6. From rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
7. On behalf of the claimants, PW-1 was examined and Exs.P1 to 13 were marked.
On behalf of respondents, RWs-1 and 2 were examined and Exs.R1 to R5 were marked.

8. The learned Trial Judge on appreciating pleadings, evidence and arguments advanced by both the sides, held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of JCB by its driver and awarded compensation of Rs.9,96,112/- with interest @ 7.5 p.a. from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount, by impugned judgment and award dated 27.11.2018.

4 9.
We have heard the arguments of the learned Advocates for both the sides.
10. The learned Advocate for appellant has vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not considered the future prospects of the deceased.
The Tribunal has also not taken into account the income of the deceased though revenue records were produced before the Tribunal, to show that he had agricultural lands.
Compensation awarded on other heads also was very meagre.

Therefore,
prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.
He has further argued that the JCB will come under the category of "Light Motor Vehicle".
Therefore, even without endorsement, if the driver drives the said vehicle, it does not amount to violation of terms and conditions of policy of insurance.
On the contrary, the driver was holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle.

Therefore,
prayed to reject the contentions of Insurer.
11. The learned Advocate for the Insurer has contended that the driver of the JCB has no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle.
As per the evidence of RW-1, JCB was weighing about 8000 kilograms and for driving the said vehicle, special license was necessary under the Motor Vehicles Act.
But, this aspect has not been considered by the Tribunal.
Ex.R3 clearly indicates that the driver had no valid and effective driving license and he was not authorized to drive the JCB.

Inspite of the evidence lead by the Insurer, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the Insurer to pay compensation though there was fundamental violation of terms and conditions of policy of insurance.

He has further contended that the Tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month, which is not proved by the claimants and though claimant Nos.2 and 3 are major sons, deduction was given to an extent of 1/3rd towards personal expenses instead of 50%.
Even the compensation awarded on the other heads are on the higher side.

He has further contended that the Tribunal has awarded interest @ 7.5% p.a. on the compensation amount, which is highly excessive and hence, prayed for interference in the said finding and also prayed to direct the respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle, to pay the compensation.
12. We have anxiously considered pleadings and evidence.

The Tribunal has considered age of the deceased as 45 years, income as Rs.8,000/- per month and multiplier as '14' and awarded compensation of Rs.9,96,112/- under the following heads:

The Tribunal in the impugned judgment, has considered age of the deceased as 45 years on the basis Smt.Yallawwa W/O Shivanappa @ Shivappa vs Chanagouda S/O Shivagouda Patil on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40348510/
5 of the age mentioned in Ex.P6.
There was no other contrary evidence, therefore, the same is to be considered.
Much was argued regarding earnings of the deceased.
It is true that claimant had produced RTCs.

The Tribunal in para Nos.15 and 16 has considered the RTC produced by the claimants and held that the RTC were not standing in the name of deceased and also do not prove that the deceased had agricultural land and was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per annum, by the agriculture and also by running the harvesting machine.
Therefore, assessed notional income of the deceased as Rs.8,000/- per month.
It does not call for any interference.

13. The Tribunal has not considered future prospects of the deceased; In the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that even in the case of agriculturist or the (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 person who had no fixed income, future prospects has to be considered, if deceased was between the age group of '40' to '50'
years, 25% of his income has to be considered as future prospects.

sentences.text: In this case, deceased was aged 45 years.
Therefore, 25% of his income shall be added towards future prospects.
Deceased left behind him, his wife and two sons.
Therefore, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Respondent No.2 had not brought out that claimants No.2 and 3 had any independent source of income.

Therefore, the contention of Respondent No.2 that claimants No.2 and 3 were majors, therefore, they cannot be considered as non-dependants and 50% of income shall be deducted towards personal expenses
is not sustainable.

On the basis of the said calculation,
the amount of compensation, for which, the claimants were entitled under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.6667X12X14= 11,20,056/-.
14.
As held in the case of Pranay Sethi (stated supra), Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram2 and N.Jayasree and Others Vs. Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Company Ltd.3

The main contention of Respondent No.2/Insurer is that the driver of JCB had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said class of vehicle and he had no special 2018 SCC Online SC 154 AIR 2021 SC 5218 license to drive JCB.
Therefore, had violated fundamental conditions of policy of insurance and hence, Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 had examined RW-1, who was ARTO of Jamakhandi, RTO office.
His evidence is very vague.

sentences.text: But there is no such serial numbers mentioned in Ex.R3.
It appears, Sl.Nos.1 to 8 mentioned in the said document pertaining to the transactions held in respect of said driving license.
RW-1 had not clarified about class of vehicle under which JCB falls.
He had not explained as to whether different licence is required to drive JCB, if it so, then under which provision of law or Motor Vehicles Act or Rules, the said licenses were issued.

He admits that the driver of the said JCB had heavy goods vehicle driving license and he could drive the vehicle having unladen weight of 45,000 kgs., and he accepted that the driver of the JCB had license to drive Bus as well as Lorry; and unladen weight of JCB was about 8,000 kgs.
16.
In the cross-examination of claimant, RW-1 has stated that JCB comes under the category of "light motor vehicle".
Ex .R3 reveals that validity of license to drive non- transport vehicle was upto 25.01.2023 and validity to drive transport vehicle was in force upto 03.06.2021.
It is not mentioned in the said document regarding the commencement of the said license or period of validity of the said license.
Therefore, on reading of Ex.R3, one could not make out that as on the date of the accident, he had no license to drive the JCB.
17. According to the evidence of RW-1, JCB comes within the category of "light motor vehicle".
The evidence of RW-1 that unladen weight of JCB is 8000 kilograms is not based on any materials on record or any other legal evidence.
RW-1 could have produced Rules or other material, which was available in his office to show that unladen weight of JCB is 8000 kilograms.
Hence, the oral evidence of RW-1 in this regard is not acceptable.
It is not in dispute that the driver of the JCB had license to drive "light motor vehicles", i.e., non- transport light motor vehicles.
Even he had license to drive Bus as well as heavy goods vehicle, which was valid upto 2021.

18. The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Shabeena Banu Vs. Shriram General,
Insurance Company Limited4 has held as under:
"The issue with regard to fastening the liability on the owner of the vehicle, on the ground that the driver of the offending had only a light motor vehicle licence and was driving a JCB, which is of a particular unladen weight, and the concept of the light motor vehicle driving licence qua the unladen weight and its validity for the purpose of the liability of the Insurer in considered".

sentences.text: For the sake of discussion, if we consider that the driver of the vehicle had no driving license to drive light motor LAWS (KAR) 2020 2 139 transport vehicle, then it does not make much difference.
Without endorsement of transport vehicle, he could drive transport vehicle.

In the similar facts and circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited5 has held at para-46 as under:
" 46(i) 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).

(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg. would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle"
as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle AIR 2017 SC (Civil) 2531 weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression 'transport vehicle'
as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.
19.
The principles of law laid down in the said judgment are applicable to the facts of the present case.

Therefore, even if there was no endorsement in respect of the said licence as 'transport vehicle',
it has to be considered that the driver of JCB had valid license to drive the said class of vehicle.

20. Rule 2(cab) of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 reads as under:
(cab) "construction equipment vehicle" means a self-propelled machine with rubber tyred (including pneumatic tyred), rubber padded or rubber or steel drum wheel mounted compactor, wheeled hydraulic excavator, wheel loader, backhoe loader,
skid-steer loader, dumper, motor grader, mobile crane, dozer and pavers with rubber track or rubber pads or wheeled pavers, fork lift truck, self-loading concrete mixer or self-propelled boom pumps, self-propelled or concrete pumps or any other construction equipment vehicle or combination thereof primarily designed to perform earth moving, excavation, loading, transportation, drilling, spreading,

8 mining, industrial undertaking, irrigation and general construction but modified and manufactured with "on or off" or "on and off" highway capabilities.

Explanation for the purpose of this clause.--A construction equipment vehicle or earthy moving vehicle shall be a non-transport vehicle the driving on the road of which is incidental to the main off-highway function and for a short duration at a speed not exceeding fifty kilometres per hour, but such vehicle does not include other purely off-highway construction equipment vehicle designed and adopted for use in any enclosed premises, factory or mine other than road network, not equipeed to travel on public roads on their own power for example slip form pavers, concrete pavers, cold milling machines, cold recycler machines and any construction equipment vehicle or earth moving vehicle with crawlers or metal track, for example, tracked excavator or excavator with legs are not considered to be falling under the scope of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, as they are not permitted to run on public roads.
(i) Reliance General Insurance Vs. Ramya JCB dated 09.11.2020.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) Divisional Manager Vs. Rangappa S/o Vaggappa Rathod 31.08.2020.

In both above cases, it was held that the driver holding licence to drive Light Motor Vehicle can drive JCB, as it comes under definition of "construction equipment vehicle".
21.

In view of the law laid down in Mukund Devangan (state supra) as well as the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Shabeena Bhanu (stated supra), it is very clear that JCB comes under the category of "construction vehicle"
and the person who has license to drive light motor non- transport vehicle can also drive the said vehicle.
Therefore, the contention of Respondent No.2/Insurer that driver of JCB had no valid license to drive the said class of vehicle is not tenable in law.
The Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on Respondent No.2/Insurer to pay the compensation.

22. The learned Advocate for Insurer, i.e., Respondent No.2 vehemently contended that the Tribunal has awarded interest @ 7.5% p.a., which is highly excessive and even the rate of interest awarded by the Bank for fixed deposit for a period of one year is less than 5%.
Therefore, prayed to reconsider the same.
There is some weight in the said submission.
The Banks, at present are granting interest on fixed deposit for a period of one year is less than 6%.
Considering the same, rate of interest has to be granted @ 6% p.a. on the enhanced amount of compensation.

23. For the aforesaid discussion, we answer the above point accordingly and pass the following:

opennyai_summary.facts:
At about, 8.30 a.m., he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Backhoe loader JCB (hereinafter will be referred as JCB for sake of brevity) by its driver.
In the said accident, Shivappa sustained grievous injuries; and while undergoing treatment, he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
4. Respondent No.1 has contended before the Trial Court that accident was not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of JCB by its driver.
The said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2, it be directed to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.2 has denied all the averments in the petition and it has contended that the owner of the vehicle has violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance and therefore, it was not liable to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
On the contrary, the driver was holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle.
Inspite of the evidence lead by the Insurer, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the Insurer to pay compensation though there was fundamental violation of terms and conditions of policy of insurance.

(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.
